input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale:
§ 9.4 standing alone meets the preferred position: Customer convenience termination of the Agreement or any Order Form on thirty days' notice, refund of prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period, and an express bar on any Vendor convenience right during a committed term. No Vendor convenience right appears anywhere else in the document.

The deviation sits in § 2.1. It binds Customer to a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay minimum "without reduction or termination rights." There is no order-of-precedence or conflict clause in the agreement, so § 2.1 (the more specific commitment) can be read to override § 9.4; at best, even if § 9.4 survives, Customer would terminate yet remain liable for the full unpaid minimum. Either way the convenience right is illusory and the effective exit cost is up to three years of committed spend — far beyond the fallback ceiling of three months' fees, and squarely in walk-away territory (no real Customer convenience right in a multi-year term).

The minimal fix preserves the commercial minimum but carves terminations out of it, so the commitment reduces pro rata and no shortfall or early-termination amount is triggered by an exit under § 9.4. § 9.4 itself needs no edit.

proposal.summary: Carve terminations out of the § 2.1 take-or-pay commitment so the § 9.4 convenience right is effective and penalty-free
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9.4 gives us a 30-day convenience termination with a pro-rata refund, but § 2.1 makes the three-year USD 2,000,000 minimum "without reduction or termination rights," which would leave us owing the full shortfall and turn that right into a penalty. We have carved terminations out of the commitment so it reduces pro rata on termination; if Copperleaf needs some recovery, we can discuss a cap not exceeding three months' Fees.

ops.oldText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: on a take-or-pay basis; provided that this commitment is reduced pro rata for, and Customer owes no shortfall, early-termination, or similar amount on account of, any termination or partial termination of this Agreement or an Order Form under § 9.4 or any other provision of this Agreement.
